mathematical_premises.scope: If A=M+F and every translated affine M-form has density cap C_M, then any slab witness of mass p=rho*ell with rho>=4C_M forces retained rough width at least p/(8C_M) on every coordinate interval box omitting total marginal probability at most p/2.

results.statement: For arbitrary cap-one probability densities on R and any finite family of bounded measurable certificates, there exist unit-measure product indicators preserving every certificate expectation exactly.

For each fixed symmetric A and interval J, arbitrary cap-one product laws and unit-measure product indicators have exactly the same attainable slab probabilities; the universal target is equivalent to the corresponding product-set interval inequality.
On bounded coordinate boxes, the bounded-kernel product optimization attains an indicator maximizer and every maximizing coordinate set is a bathtub best response to its fiber score.

Applying account02/B13's slab-mass-trimmed theorem to exact product indicators yields an all-deletion-budget concentration-radius inequality in the current rank-one-plus-four-diagonal rough normal form.

next_step: Exploit the coordinatewise best-response threshold equations together with the all-budget trimmed quantile-radius lower bound to control the rough diagonal-plus-secondary-rank-one phase without intervalizing the product sets or deleting coefficient-small quadratic terms.
